name: Tower Route

pitch_detail.notes: Ascend the prominent gully on the NE side to the first tower
Work west onto and up the first tower
Rappel into the notch between towers
Continue climbing the remaining two towers
Long, steep, exposed snowfield leads to the summit

rappel_detail.notes: One rappel into the notch between the first and second towers. On the descent parties reverse the towers, rappelling where needed, or downclimb to the notch system used on the ascent.
rappel_detail.anchor: not described; carry slings and cord
rappel_detail.station: The first tower, above the notch that separates it from the second tower.

rappels: One rappel into the notch between the first and second towers
approach: Approach via the Big Four Ice Caves trail from the Big Four Picnic Area / Ice Caves Trailhead, then traverse toward the north side of the mountain to reach the base of the first tower's gully.
overview: A technical rock-and-snow line on the mountain's north side/NE ridge that climbs a prominent gully to the first of three rock towers, works over and between the towers via rock climbing and a rappel into a notch, then finishes up a long, steep, exposed snowfield to the summit.
beta: First climbed July 25, 1972 by Ben Guydelkon and Ron Miller as a new line on Big Four's north side. From the end of the ice-caves trail, the party traversed to the northeast side of the first tower to a prominent gully; climbing this gully let them work west onto and up the first tower. They rappelled into a notch, climbed two more towers, then finished with rock scrambling leading to a long, steep, exposed snowfield to the summit.
fa: Ben Guydelkon and Ron Miller, July 25, 1972
